God's Eye View: Real‑time 3D Global Simulator Brings Public Data to Your Browser

04 Nov 2026, 06:37 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: github.com

2 min read

Key takeaways

Image: GitHub · Photo source · Resized and letterboxed to 16:9; no AI generation

In this article
  1. Overview
  2. Key Features
  3. Technical Details
  4. Practical Implications

Overview

  • What it is: An open‑source web app that renders a photorealistic 3D globe and overlays live information from aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes, traffic and public cameras.
  • Confirmed: The project is hosted on GitHub under the repository bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view.
  • Reported: It is described as a “spy‑satellite simulator” that uses publicly available feeds.
  • Unknown: The exact number of data sources and their update frequency are not disclosed.

Key Features

  • Live Layers: Real‑time aircraft tracking, vessel monitoring, orbital data, seismic activity and camera feeds.
  • Hands‑free Interaction: Voice‑controlled AI agent that can answer location queries and provide context.
  • Sensor Styles: Multiple visual modes (CRT, NVG, FLIR/thermal, Noir) that change how the globe appears.
  • 3D Models: Detailed aircraft models for major types and dynamic swapping as you approach.
  • Shareable Views: URLs that preserve camera angle, style, active layers and tracked targets.
  • Reset Globe: One‑click return to a full Earth view.

Technical Details

  • Platform: Runs locally in a browser; no account or API keys required for basic layers.
  • Setup: Can be installed via Pinokio or run from the terminal; optional keys unlock photorealistic rendering and additional services.
  • Data Sources: Uses aggregated public data; traffic simulation is based on location aggregates, while camera and launch data are coarse estimates.
  • Performance: Benchmarked at ~1.86 seconds cold start on a typical machine; performance varies with hardware and network.

Practical Implications

  • Accessibility: Anyone with a modern browser can explore global activity without specialized hardware.
  • Transparency: All code is inspectable, allowing users to verify how data is collected and displayed.
  • Potential Uses: Educational demonstrations, situational awareness, and informal monitoring of public signals.
  • Limitations: Some feeds are approximations; precise real‑world accuracy depends on the underlying public data quality.

How to Verify the Original Announcement

  • Visit the GitHub repository to examine the source code and documentation.
  • Check the project’s release notes or changelog for updates on data feeds and new features.
  • Test the live demo in a browser to confirm that the described layers appear as advertised.
  • Review community discussions or issue trackers for known bugs and data gaps.

Conclusion

God's Eye View offers a unique window into publicly available global activity by combining a realistic 3D globe with a variety of live data layers. Its open‑source nature and low barrier to entry make it a valuable tool for anyone interested in spatial intelligence, while users should be aware of the inherent approximations in the underlying feeds.
